# Tobit Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_012_page_001.jpg

---

**12:1** Then Tobit called his son Tobias and said to him, "See to it, my child, that you give the man who went with you his wages, and add something beyond what was agreed."

**12:2** And he said, "Father, how much shall I give him? It would not hurt me to give him half of everything he helped me bring back;

**12:3** for he led me safely, he healed my wife, he brought the silver back with me, and he healed you as well."

**12:4** And the old man said, "He deserves to receive half of all that he brought back."

**12:5** So he called him and said, "Take half of all that you brought, and go in peace."

**12:6** Then he called them both aside privately and said to them, "Bless God and give thanks before all the living for the good things he has done for you, so that they may bless and sing praises to his name. Proclaim the words of God with honor, and do not grow negligent in giving thanks to him.

**12:7** It is good to guard the secret of a king, but the works of God — these are to be proclaimed gloriously and praised. Do what is good, and evil will not overtake you.

**12:8** Prayer with fasting is good, and almsgiving with righteousness. Better is a little with righteousness than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to hoard gold.

**12:9** For almsgiving delivers from death and purges away every sin. Those who give alms and live righteously will be filled with life;

**12:10** but those who sin are enemies of their own life.

**12:11** "I will no longer hide the truth from you. I said and kept hidden: it is good to guard a king's secret, but the works of God it is honorable to proclaim gloriously.

**12:12** Now hear this: when you prayed — you and Sarah your daughter-in-law — I carried the memorial of your prayer before the Holy One; and when you were burying the dead,

**12:13** and when you left your meal and went without hesitation to wrap the dead man, I was sent to test you.

**12:14** And at the same time God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law.

**12:15** I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the holy ones and enter before the Glory of the Holy One."

**12:16** And they were both troubled, and they fell upon their faces, for they were afraid.

**12:17** And he said to them, "Do not fear; peace be with you. Bless God through all the ages.

**12:18** For it was not of my own accord that I came to you, but by the will of our God. Therefore bless him all your days; praise him.

**12:19** "You were seeing me eat — but what you saw was a vision.

**12:20** And now give thanks to God, for I am ascending to him who sent me. Write everything that has happened in a scroll."

**12:21** They rose up, and they could no longer see him.

**12:22** And they continued blessing God and singing hymns to him; and they gave thanks to God for these great works of his: that an angel of God had appeared to them.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

**Verse 15 — The Angelophany Formula:** All three agents rightly recognized this as the theological summit of the book. LOGOS and EMET preserve "the Glory of the Holy One" (*enōpion tēs doxēs tou Hagiou*) as a reverential circumlocution; PNEUMA renders it more directly but still captures the grandeur. Consensus preserves "the Glory of the Holy One" — the indirect language is theologically intentional and historically significant (kavod tradition).

**Verses 8–9 — *Eleēmosyna*:** EMET preserves the Greek transliteration; LOGOS and PNEUMA render it "almsgiving." Consensus uses "almsgiving" for readability while noting the richer semantic range in the Disagreement Log. The three-part triad (prayer / fasting / almsgiving) is kept structurally parallel.

**Verse 7 — King's secret proverb:** All three agents handle this similarly. The contrast structure (conceal vs. proclaim) is well preserved. Consensus follows LOGOS's rendering.

**Verse 19 — Vision clarification:** EMET's "it was a vision you were seeing" is the most literal; LOGOS's "you were seeing a vision" is cleanest; PNEUMA's "what you saw was a vision" is most natural. Consensus takes PNEUMA here.

**Verse 13 — "without hesitation":** LOGOS adds this phrase drawing on the fuller narrative context of Tobit's burial acts; EMET does not have it; PNEUMA has "every act of faithfulness." Consensus retains "without hesitation" as contextually defensible.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Decision |
|-------|------|-------|--------|-----------------|
| 12:1 | "See, my-child, to give the-wage" | "See to it, my child, that you give...his wages" | "make sure you pay...what he's owed" | LOGOS — clearest |
| 12:5 | "go in-health" | "go in peace" | "Go well, friend" | LOGOS — "go in peace" is standard farewell |
| 12:6 | "make-known gloriously" | "Proclaim the words of God with honor" | "Shout God's deeds from the rooftops" | LOGOS — PNEUMA too paraphrastic |
| 12:8 | "eleēmosyna" (untranslated) | "almsgiving" | "Giving to those in need" | LOGOS — "almsgiving" is the established term |
| 12:9 | "Those-who-do eleēmosyna and righteousness" | "Those who give alms and live righteously" | "Those who are merciful, who live justly" | LOGOS — faithful to Greek |
| 12:11 | "I-have-said and I-have-hidden" | "I have spoken and I have kept it hidden" | "I can't keep the truth from you any longer" | LOGOS — preserves the formal structure |
| 12:13 | no "without hesitation" | "without hesitation" | "every act of faithfulness" | LOGOS |
| 12:15 | "holy-angels who-present the-prayers" | "holy angels who present the prayers" | "seven holy angels who stand in the presence" | LOGOS/EMET — PNEUMA loses the intercessory detail |
| 12:18 | "not of my-[own] grace" | "not of my own accord" | "not...on my own initiative" | LOGOS |
| 12:19 | "it-was a-vision you-were-seeing" | "you were seeing a vision" | "What you saw was a vision" | PNEUMA — most natural |
| 12:20 | "ascending to-the-one-who-sent me" | "ascending to him who sent me" | "returning to the one who sent me" | LOGOS — "ascending" preserves the angelological register |
| 12:22 | "a-messenger of God appeared" | "an angel of God had appeared" | "an angel of God had appeared in the flesh" | LOGOS — "in the flesh" is PNEUMA's addition, not in source |
